item.title: WHO staff evacuated from DR Congo hospital after sheltering for over three days amid fierce fighting: WHO chief
item.description: World Health Organisation staff and DRC Health Ministry officials were safely evacuated on Tuesday after sheltering for over three days inside an Akwe hospital in Ituri Province amid fierce conflict.
item.content:encoded:
WHO staff evacuated from DR Congo hospital after sheltering for over three days amid fierce fighting: WHO chief World Health Organisation staff and DRC Health Ministry officials were safely evacuated on Tuesday after sheltering for over three days inside an Akwe hospital in Ituri Province amid fierce conflict. WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus also announced the temporary relocation of its Ebola team from Mongbwalu due to rising insecurity. ANI | Updated: 24-11-2026 22:59 IST | Created: 24-11-2026 22:59 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

World Health Organisation (WHO) personnel, officials from the Health Ministry of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and fellow responders have been safely evacuated after spending over three days sheltering inside a hospital in Akwe in Ituri Province amid fierce conflict, WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus announced on Tuesday. Sharing the update on X, Tedros wrote, "WHO staff, DRC Ministry of Health and other colleagues have been safely evacuated from the hospital in Akwe, Ituri Province, where they were sheltering amid fierce conflict for over three days. They have been brought to safety thanks to combined efforts across health, government and humanitarian partners under very challenging circumstances. My thanks to everyone involved in this operation." The WHO Director-General further noted that the global health agency has temporarily withdrawn its Ebola response team from Mongbwalu following escalating security threats in the region. "Because of the increased insecurity in Mongbwalu, we have also temporarily relocated the Ebola team of WHO staff and partners until the situation calms. We reiterate once again: health care, health workers, Ebola responders and humanitarians must be protected at all times!" he stated. Earlier on Sunday, Tedros had reported that WHO personnel and response partners were forced to take shelter inside a maternity ward of a hospital in Ituri for more than 24 hours as heavy fighting raged nearby. "Heavy fighting has been ongoing since yesterday in the vicinity of a hospital in Ituri, in an area close to where the Ebola outbreak first emerged. As a result, colleagues and response partners have been sheltering for their lives in a maternity ward of the facility for over 24 hours," Tedros had posted on X at the time. He had warned that the hostilities severely hampered both hospital operations and the broader Ebola containment efforts, placing patients, families and medical staff in serious danger. "Across Eastern DRC, the frequency of attacks has increased since the end of October, seriously affecting the Ebola response," he had added. (ANI)

item.title: Putin warns Ukraine over targeting energy facilities, says "retaliatory actions inevitable"
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Tuesday warned Ukraine that Moscow's retaliatory response to attacks on Russian fuel and energy infrastructure was inevitable, asserting that Kyiv's continued ...
item.content:encoded:
Putin warns Ukraine over targeting energy facilities, says "retaliatory actions inevitable" Russian President Vladimir Putin on Tuesday warned Ukraine that Moscow's retaliatory response to attacks on Russian fuel and energy infrastructure was inevitable, asserting that Kyiv's continued strikes would not inflict critical damage on Russia. ANI | Updated: 24-11-2026 22:50 IST | Created: 24-11-2026 22:50 IST

Russian President Vladimir Putin (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

Russia

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Russian President Vladimir Putin on Tuesday warned Ukraine that Moscow's retaliatory response to attacks on Russian fuel and energy infrastructure was inevitable, asserting that Kyiv's continued strikes would not inflict critical damage on Russia. According to Russian state media TASS, Putin, speaking at the opening of a meeting of the Commission on Fuel and Energy Complex (FEC) Development Strategy and Environmental Safety, said Russia would respond to attacks targeting its energy facilities. "I would like to point out that retaliatory actions on our part are inevitable. Everyone should know this," Putin said. The Russian President also accused Kyiv of continuing attacks on Russian oil refineries and processing facilities despite US President Donald Trump's request to refrain from targeting such infrastructure. "We see that the Kyiv regime continues its attacks on our processing facilities, despite the US President's call and direct request to refrain from these attacks. But the Kyiv authorities are not heeding such advice. Everything continues as if nothing happened," Putin said. Putin further stated that the escalation of attacks initiated by Ukraine in early June, which was publicly outlined as a 40-day plan, would not cause critical damage to Russia's energy infrastructure. "We, for our part, have said repeatedly and understand that the escalation initiated by the enemy at the beginning of June of this year and planned, as was publicly stated, for 40 days, is not capable of inflicting critical damage on us," he said. Addressing Russia's energy trade and export strategy, Putin said Moscow would seek to expand its markets and maintain cooperation with reliable international partners despite efforts to restrict Russian energy supplies. "We, in turn, will expand our sales markets and cooperate with predictable, responsible partners," the Russian President said. He also highlighted measures taken by the Russian government to safeguard domestic fuel supplies, including restrictions on exports of gasoline, aviation fuel and diesel, with certain exceptions for supplies agreed upon with the United States. "The export of gasoline, jet fuel, and diesel fuel was restricted, with the exception of partial deliveries to global markets, as we agreed with the President of the United States of America," Putin said. He added that an import damper mechanism had been introduced and exchange regulations governing the sale of gasoline and diesel fuel had been adjusted. Putin also criticised continued European efforts to restrict Russian energy exports, warning that such measures would have consequences for European countries themselves. "We see ongoing attempts to restrict Russian energy exports to Europe. I've noted it repeatedly, and today it's obvious, as they say, that such actions have serious consequences, but first and foremost for the Europeans themselves," he said. "They will have less of our oil and gas, but more problems," Putin added. The remarks came as Putin addressed the impact of attacks on Russia's energy infrastructure, the country's fuel security and its strategy for maintaining energy exports amid restrictions on Russian supplies. (ANI)

item.title: Four oil tankers explode, catch fire after hitting naval mines in Hormuz: Iran's Navy
item.description: Four oil tankers have exploded and caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, according to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy and the Navy of its Armed ...
item.content:encoded:
Four oil tankers explode, catch fire after hitting naval mines in Hormuz: Iran's Navy Four oil tankers have exploded and caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, according to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy and the Navy of its Armed Forces, amid heightened tensions over maritime movement through the strategic waterway. ANI | Updated: 24-11-2026 22:18 IST | Created: 24-11-2026 22:18 IST

Representative Image (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

Iran

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Four oil tankers have exploded and caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, according to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy and the Navy of its Armed Forces, amid heightened tensions over maritime movement through the strategic waterway. According to statements issued by the IRGC Navy's Public Relations and carried by the Iranian state broadcaster Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting (IRIB), an oil tanker travelling through the Strait of Hormuz earlier today struck a naval mine and exploded, catching fire east of the waterway. The IRGC Navy further said that two other tankers were forced to return to the Persian Gulf after witnessing the explosion and receiving a radio warning from its Strait of Hormuz Traffic Control Centre. "The IRGC Navy warns: Traveling through fake and unauthorized routes will result in nothing but explosions and fires for violators," the IRGC Navy said in its statement. In a separate statement, carried by IRIB, the Iranian Navy's Public Relations Department reported that two other oil tankers had caught fire after entering a restricted area east of the Strait of Hormuz. According to the Iranian Navy, the vessels had disabled their identification and navigation systems before entering the restricted zone and subsequently struck naval mines, leaving them unable to move. "The Strait of Hormuz will never open until Iran's goals and demands are met, and tanker owners are required to coordinate with the armed forces for safe passage through this strategic strait," the Iranian Navy said. Meanwhile, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) reported a separate incident in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, stating that three vessels had been struck by unidentified projectiles while transiting eastbound. In its incident report, UKMTO said it had received a delayed report of the incident, which occurred at approximately 2025 UTC. "The verified report stated that three vessels were struck by unknown projectiles whilst transiting eastbound. The vessels continued their transits and all crew have been accounted for. Damage assessment and environmental impact unknown at present," the UKMTO report stated. UKMTO advised vessels operating in the area to exercise caution and report any suspicious activity while authorities investigate the incident. The latest developments come amid continuing tensions in West Asia over maritime movement through the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran warning tanker operators against using unauthorised routes and insisting that vessels coordinate with its armed forces for safe passage. (ANI)

item.title: Houthi attack on Riyadh Financial Centre in Saudi injures 11 people, including two Indians
item.description: Eleven people, including two Indian nationals, were injured after one of the towers of the Financial Centre in Saudi Arabia's capital, Riyadh, was targeted in an attack allegedly carried out by ...
item.content:encoded:
Houthi attack on Riyadh Financial Centre in Saudi injures 11 people, including two Indians Eleven people, including two Indian nationals, were injured after one of the towers of the Financial Centre in Saudi Arabia's capital, Riyadh, was targeted in an attack allegedly carried out by Yemen's Houthis, the Saudi Civil Defence said on Tuesday. ANI | Updated: 24-11-2026 21:35 IST | Created: 24-11-2026 21:35 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Eleven people, including two Indian nationals, were injured after one of the towers of the Financial Centre in Saudi Arabia's capital, Riyadh, was targeted in an attack allegedly carried out by Yemen's Houthis, the Saudi Civil Defence said on Tuesday. In a statement on X, the General Directorate of Saudi Civil Defence said that the injured also included two Saudi citizens, three Nepalese nationals and four Egyptian nationals. "The Civil Defence responded to an incident in which one of the towers of the Financial Centre in the city of Riyadh was subjected to a terrorist attack by the terrorist Houthi militia, resulting in (11) injuries. They are: two citizens, two residents of Indian nationality, (3) residents of Nepalese nationality, and (4) residents of Egyptian nationality," the Saudi Civil Defence said. It further said that relevant authorities acted immediately following the incident, initiating prescribed emergency response measures to protect lives and property. "The competent authorities responded to the incident immediately upon its occurrence, implemented all approved procedures and measures for dealing with such cases, and took the necessary steps to ensure the safety of lives and property," the statement added. The Saudi-led coalition's official spokesperson for coalition forces also confirmed the targeting of a tower at the Financial Centre, describing it as a "terrorist attack". "The Coalition:- One of the towers of the Financial Centre was targeted in a cowardly terrorist attack.- The relevant authorities are conducting an on-site investigation at the scene of the attack," the spokesperson said in a post on X. The incident comes amid heightened tensions between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthi authorities following allegations of Saudi-led coalition airstrikes in Yemen's Al-Hudaydah Governorate. In a statement posted on Telegram on Monday, Yemen's Ministry of Communications and Information Technology accused Saudi-led coalition aircraft of carrying out airstrikes on telecommunications buildings, workers' accommodation and a mosque in the governorate. The Houthi-controlled ministry said that the strikes killed 17 workers and injured 11 others as an initial toll while causing extensive destruction to telecommunications infrastructure. "The Ministry of Communications and Information Technology condemns in the strongest terms the heinous crime committed by Saudi-led coalition aircraft at dawn today, Monday, 14 Jumada al-Akhirah 1448 AH, corresponding to November 23, 2026 AD, with a number of raids targeting telecommunications buildings in Al-Hudaydah Governorate, which resulted in the martyrdom of 17 workers and the injury of 11 others, as an initial toll," the statement said. The ministry further alleged that the strikes completely destroyed telecommunications facilities, including administrative buildings, workers' housing, a mosque, a communications site and a tower. It also claimed that the damage disrupted telecommunications and internet services in several districts of the governorate, depriving tens of thousands of people of basic communication services. (ANI)
